blogs.title: The Silent Desaturation: When 'Ondine's Curse' Isn't Congenital
blogs.description: This post explores the pathophysiology of acquired central hypoventilation in Chiari Malformation Type I (CMI). It analyzes the critical dissociation between voluntary and automatic breathing controls, explaining why patients can experience profound hypoxia (SpO2 70-80%) without dyspnea or respiratory distress. We will discuss the mechanism of brainstem compression disrupting afferent interoceptive pathways and why standard pulmonary workups often miss this diagnosis.

blogs.title: Choking on Nothing: The Neurogenic Dysphagia Blind Spot
blogs.description: Focusing on the diagnostic odyssey of the patient's 7-year history of choking, this article argues for earlier neurological evaluation in cases of 'unexplained' dysphagia. It contrasts neurogenic dysphagia (affecting solids and liquids equally due to lower cranial nerve nucleus compression) with mechanical or motility disorders like GERD. The post provides a framework for clinicians to recognize when repeated normal ENT/GI scopes should trigger a search for posterior fossa pathology rather than further GI investigation.

blogs.title: Radiology Retrospective: The Danger of the 'Normal' Report in Post-Traumatic Headaches
blogs.description: Using the case's 14-year diagnostic delay as a cautionary tale, this post emphasizes the necessity of clinician-led image review over reliance solely on radiologist reports. It details specific signs of a crowded foramen magnum and tonsillar ectopia that are frequently overlooked on non-contrast CT scans performed for trauma. The discussion includes the controversial link between minor head trauma and the unmasking or exacerbation of congenital Chiari malformations.

blogs.title: Beyond the Valsalva Headache: Atypical Pain Presentations in Chiari Syndrome
blogs.description: While occipital headaches worsened by Valsalva are the hallmark of CMI, this post dives into atypical pain phenotypes, specifically the patient's unique vertex allodynia ('burning vertex') relieved only by cutting her hair. We examine the overlap between occipital neuralgia, small fiber neuropathy, and cervicomedullary compression, urging clinicians to consider structural causes even when headache distribution does not fit classic migraine or tension-type profiles.

blogs.title: The AHI Trap: Why Standard Sleep Studies Underestimate Central Apnea in Brainstem Compression
blogs.description: This technical deep-dive addresses the limitations of Type III home sleep apnea tests in diagnosing central hypoventilation syndromes. It explains how the lack of EEG leads to an artificially low Apnea-Hypopnea Index (AHI) by including wake time in the denominator, potentially masking severe central events. The post advocates for full Type I polysomnography with capnography for patients with suspected brainstem pathology despite 'mild' home study results.
